attestations.source_text: The passé composé is one of the tenses colloquially used in French to talk about past events. It is built of two parts: the auxiliary or helping verb, avoir or être, + a past participle.
Most verbs in the passé composé are conjugated with avoir.
Many verbs conjugated with avoir in the passé composé have irregular past participles that you simply have to learn by heart.
Some verbs use être instead of avoir in the passé composé. It is very important to memorize the (finite) list of verbs conjugated with être.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Past participle agreement with preceding direct object
exceptions_and_traps.description: With avoir, past participle does not normally agree, but agrees with a direct object that precedes the verb.

attestations.source_text: In the passé composé of verbs conjugated with avoir, the past participle agrees with the direct object of the verb, but only in sentences where the direct object noun or pronoun precedes the verb.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Pronominal verbs: no agreement with direct object/verb following
exceptions_and_traps.description: Past participle does not agree with subject when the pronominal verb is followed by a direct object or another verb.

attestations.section_title: Pronominal verbs in the passé composé
attestations.source_text: Note that the past participle does not agree with the subject of the pronominal verb when the verb is followed by a direct object or by another verb.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Reciprocal verbs: no agreement with indirect object
exceptions_and_traps.description: For reciprocal pronominal verbs, if the reciprocal pronoun is an indirect object, the past participle does not agree.

attestations.section_title: Pronominal verbs in the passé composé
attestations.source_text: When reciprocal verbs take an indirect object in French, the past participle does not agree.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Verbs with être or avoir (six verbs)
exceptions_and_traps.description: Sortir, rentrer, monter, descendre, passer, retourner use avoir when transitive; meaning changes.

attestations.section_title: Verbs conjugated with avoir or être
attestations.source_text: Six verbs among those conjugated with être in the passé composé (sortir, rentrer, monter, descendre, passer, retourner) are conjugated with avoir and follow the avoir agreement when a direct object follows the verb. In these cases, the meaning of the verb has changed.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Forgetting agreement with être verbs
exceptions_and_traps.description: Past participle must agree with subject when using être; common to forget -e/-s.

attestations.source_text: The past participle of verbs conjugated with être agrees in gender and number with the subject.
